title: A Day in the Life: 82nd ERQS Parachute Rigger-No Graphics
description: Aircrew Flight Equipment Airmen deployed to the 82nd Expeditionary Rescue Squadron at Camp Lemonnier, Djibouti, work day and night behind the scenes to ensure the safety of our rescue Airmen. Part of their job is packing parachutes, which takes extraordinary attention to detail and is an essential part of supporting Combined Joint Task Force-Horn of Africa rescue operations in East Africa. Here is an inside view of what they do to ensure each parachute is ready to go at a moments notice.
keywords: parachute rigger, AFE, Aircrew Flight Equipment, 82nd ERQS, Africa, rescue, Djibouti

transcript.text: - I'm Staff Sergeant Antonio.
I'm a parachute rigger with aircrew flight equipment.
When you're in a theater like this,
you never know what type of mission might arise.
Some of those missions do involve having to jump
out of an airplane to go and do some type of rescue
and in those situations they need to have
parachutes ready and on hand and we try to maintain
as much of an alert stocked system for them,
so they have what they need when they need it.
On an average day here, we're trying to stay ahead
of our equipment cycle.
Inspection cycles that can be anything
from managing oxygen equipment
to packing full blown rigs.
It's an honor.
You never know which pack job is gonna be
the one that's gonna save somebody's life,
so you take them all with the same level
of seriousness and respect.
